smt-2018-discrete-tiebreaker-01.title: Shape of $n$
smt-2018-discrete-tiebreaker-01.body:
Having $6=2\cdot3$ factors means $n=ab^2$ for primes $a,b$ (or $p^5$, which cannot have $55$ as a factor). Since $55=5\cdot11\mid n$, the primes are $5$ and $11$. If $n=11\cdot5^2=275$ the factors are $1,5,11,25,55,275$ and $55$ is only the 2nd largest. If $n=5\cdot11^2=605$ the factors are $1,5,11,55,121,605$, and $55$ is the 3rd largest.

**Answer: 605**

smt-2018-discrete-tiebreaker-02.title: Last digit is forced
smt-2018-discrete-tiebreaker-02.body:
The digits can only be $1,\ldots,8$ ($0$ and $9$ are divisible by $9$). Let $a_k$ be the number of $k$-digit strings from $\{1,\ldots,8\}$ with digit sum divisible by $9$, and $b_k$ the number that are not. For any residue class of the first $k-1$ digits not $\equiv0$ there is exactly one last digit in $1..8$ giving a total $\equiv0$; if the first $k-1$ digits already sum to $0\pmod 9$ there is none. So $a_k=b_{k-1}$ and $b_k=7b_{k-1}+8a_{k-1}$ (a non-multiple has $8$ choices, one of which makes a multiple; a multiple has $8$ choices, all of which give non-multiples).

$a_1=0,\ b_1=8$; $a_2=8,\ b_2=56$; $a_3=56,\ b_3=7\cdot56+8\cdot8=456$; $a_4=456,\ b_4=7\cdot456+8\cdot56=3640$; $a_5=3640$.

**Answer: 3640**

smt-2018-discrete-tiebreaker-03.title: Swap the order of counting
smt-2018-discrete-tiebreaker-03.body:
Count pairs $(s,\text{removal})$. A removal is determined by which $2n$ of the $10$ positions are kept ($\binom{10}{2n}$ ways), the kept characters must then be the regular string of length $2n$, and the other $10-2n$ characters are free ($2^{10-2n}$ ways). So the total is $\sum_{n=1}^5\binom{10}{2n}2^{10-2n}=45\cdot256+210\cdot64+210\cdot16+45\cdot4+1=11520+13440+3360+180+1=28501$.

**Answer: 28501**
